newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans surge higher on weather forecasts.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans surge higher on weather forecasts.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures opened sharply higher on Monday, led by new crop on forecasts for another hot, dry spell for the U.S. Midwest, traders said.

Meteorologists said a warm front would hit the U.S. Midwest this weekend, bringing another patch of hot, dry weather. Long-range forecasts suggested the heat wave would persist through early next week.
But gains in the nearbys were limited by talk China defaulted on a purchase of 150,000 tonnes of U.S. soymeal and profit taking on the bull spreads.
Pit sources said buying was broad-based early.
Merrill Lynch, Refco Inc, ADM and Smith Barney were said to be buyers of the November.
At 0954 CDT, soybeans were up 18-3/4 to 5-1/2 cents per bushel with November up 18-3/4 at $6.20 a bushel.
